caption: The drawing shows a group of people arranged in a horizontal composition, centering around a figure who has fallen to the ground under the weight of a large wooden cross. This central figure, with a crown of thorns and a brown robe, is lying on the ground with the cross resting on his back. Two figures in blue and red attire are pulling ropes attached to the fallen figure, while several others, dressed in colored garments such as red, green, and brown, stand nearby holding spears. Among the surrounding figures are people with halos, dressed in garments of red, blue, and green, suggesting a religious scene. There are also figures wearing helmets and pointed hats, and a horse is visible on the left side. The background is filled with overlapping heads and faces, and the primary colors used in the drawing are earthy browns, muted reds, blues, greens, and hints of gold for the halos. The drawing has a flat perspective, and all figures are stylized with elongated facial features and hands.
title: Station of the Cross No. 9: Jesus Falls the Third Time
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
